pr_title: Shield service call from cancellation on REST API connection loss
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change

When calling a service from REST API, the service used to be cancelled on connection drop. If you relied on that behavior, you would need to revisit the logic. With this change, a connection drop will not cancel the service call. Additionally, if the service call takes more than 10 second to execute, the REST API will return and the service call will continue executing in the background. Although this behavior is documented, it was not the case for several past releases.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

This PR restores the behavior in the [REST API documentation](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/api/rest/): when a service call is executed via `/api/services/<domain>/<service>`, the call should return when the service has been executed or after 10 seconds, whichever comes first.
Also, this PR fixes the cancellation of the service call on disconnect.

issue_context.title: Automation is cancelled on API client disconnect
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have a problem with my automations being cancelled during wait timer.
Background: I have a backup server that should stay powered off most of the time, only powering on at night to make a backup.
The power socket is controlled by home assistant. It has automation.backup_watchdog that waits for 31 minutes and powers off the server. While the server is running, it uses web API to restart the automation at a regular intervals while the OS is still running to prevent it to power off too early.
The error I have is that the automation mysteriously gets cancelled after about 6 minutes of waiting (out of 31), even when it is not restarted.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.9.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

automation

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/automation/basics/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
id: '1668363102805'
alias: Backup watchdog
description: Backup watchdog
trigger:
  - platform: device
    type: changed_states
    device_id: 14c5be6c720fb48ea6daf7d4dfa7dcfc
    entity_id: light.sonoff_10013f38ac_1
    domain: light
  - platform: homeassistant
    event: start
  - platform: event
    event_type: automation_reloaded
    enabled: true
condition:
  - condition: template
    value_template: >-
      {{trigger is not defined or trigger.platform != "event" or
      trigger.event.event_type != "automation_reloaded" or
      this.attributes.current == 0}}
    alias: Only trigger if this automation has been reloaded
action:
  - condition: device
    type: is_on
    device_id: 14c5be6c720fb48ea6daf7d4dfa7dcfc
    entity_id: light.sonoff_10013f38ac_1
    domain: light
    alias: Cancel watchdog timer if backup is off
  - service: notify.persistent_notification
    data:
      message: Watchdog refreshed
      title: Test
    enabled: false
  - delay:
      hours: 0
      minutes: 31
      seconds: 0
      milliseconds: 0
  - type: turn_off
    device_id: 14c5be6c720fb48ea6daf7d4dfa7dcfc
    entity_id: light.sonoff_10013f38ac_1
    domain: light
    enabled: true
  - service: notify.persistent_notification
    data:
      message: Turning off backup
      title: Test
    enabled: false
mode: restart
```

After a bit of debugging I've found a clue.
It turns out that when an automation is started via REST API `services/automation/trigger`, it will be running until the connection is broken. However in my case the automation is what is responsible to switch off the backup server power after it shuts down, and the `curl` process is terminated during the shutdown.
This is probably related to the introduction of a service responses or an aiohttp update.

To quote the [documentation](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/api/rest/):

> 
> `POST` `/api/services/<domain>/<service>` 🔒
> Calls a service within a specific domain. Will return when the service has been executed or after 10 seconds, whichever comes first.

This is not what I am experiencing now. The call does not return until the service call is finished, and when the client drops the connection, the `asyncio.CancelledError` is raised that cancels the automation.

Please advise.
The `aiohttp` version I have is 3.8.5 and https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/pull/6727 is already there
I don't know how the whole rest API works, but maybe you can consider using a webhook as trigger?

But we already know it hasn't been completed, because we haven't provided the value for the future yet, and later we verify that the value is used. But if you believe an additional assert will be more readable, I will add it.
We think that it should work that way. To prove it, we should assert. There's a difference.
This means it could run forever and never timeout which might block shutdown

If I understand it correctly, it will be cancelled on stage 3 of shutdown. It is only shielded from cancellation from within the `api` component. That is, if the integration providing the service does not cancel it earlier on `homeassistant_stop` event.
We would still have to wait the whole timeout of stage 1 and stage 2
I think what you want is to shield the current task from cancelation but run the service call in another task

> I think what you want is to shield the current task from cancelation but run the service call in another task

What I want is for the service call to be independent from the source that calls it.
Please correct me if I am wrong, but it feels redundant, because services are internally run in a separate task anyway, so it's a task in a task.
[hass.services.async_call()](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/1a6184a9aaae04bb28a53ac0fcdf1f75cf6ea9aa/homeassistant/core.py#L1966) calls [ServiceRegistry._execute_service()](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/1a6184a9aaae04bb28a53ac0fcdf1f75cf6ea9aa/homeassistant/core.py#L2087), which creates a new task using [hass.async_add_executor_job()](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/1a6184a9aaae04bb28a53ac0fcdf1f75cf6ea9aa/homeassistant/core.py#L630).

> We would still have to wait the whole timeout of stage 1 and stage 2

This is up to the integration that provides the service. It could be desirable or not for different integrations.
For example, the `automation` integration does not stop any automations while on stage 1 and stage 2, it even allows to start new automations when we enter stage 1 of shutdown, so it is desirable for some automations to run until stage 3. If we use `api` integration to call a service that triggers an automation, it should behave the same way as triggered by other means. We are not affecting the shutdown here, at least not more than a manually executed service.
Other integrations, if desired, will listen to the `homeassistant_stop` event and will cancel their tasks regardless of the source of the service call. The `shield()` will not prevent a task to be canceled from within. Also, `shield()` will not prevent the `api` component itself to shutdown.

The task isn't being canceled from within though, it's being canceled by the timeout context manager when it hits the timeout

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/102685c4c8481ec5d9c132fcf06b46057e815969/Lib/asyncio/timeouts.py#L123C9-L123C9

I think it would be fine to use async_create_task instead of making it a background task if you didn't want it to be canceled at shutdown.  

I don't see a good way to avoid creating a task without the shield blocking the inner cancellation when the timeout happens

> which creates a new task using hass.async_add_executor_job().

This function doesn't create a task

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/1a6184a9aaae04bb28a53ac0fcdf1f75cf6ea9aa/homeassistant/core.py#L634

The above names the return a task but it's actually a future https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/21c8fbf28dda1f338303295b094b9cc365d101b2/Lib/asyncio/base_events.py#L859

https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-eventloop.html#asyncio.loop.run_in_executor

> This function doesn't create a task

Ok, I may be wrong with the terminology, but whatever it is, it is added to `hass._tasks` and is [cancelled](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/1a6184a9aaae04bb28a53ac0fcdf1f75cf6ea9aa/homeassistant/core.py#L865) on stage 3 of shutdown, i.e. at the same time it would have been cancelled if the service was called by the other means. A background task is [cancelled](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/1a6184a9aaae04bb28a53ac0fcdf1f75cf6ea9aa/homeassistant/core.py#L815) a little bit too early.

> The task isn't being canceled from within though, it's being canceled by the timeout context manager when it hits the timeout

Sorry for the misunderstanding. What I mean is that at shutdown it will be cancelled from within and `shield` won't prevent the shutdown. On timeout, the `shield` would be cancelled, but the service would continue as normal.

> I don't see a good way to avoid creating a task without the shield blocking the inner cancellation when the timeout happens

I have tested my solution and it works with both shutdown and shielding the service from either timeout or connection drop. To test shutdown I triggered an automation that waits for 31 minutes.

Let's pull in the test change from https://github.com/home-assistant/core/commit/56033fa2cbed8e70a3d7cbaa4500a675f8310dbb#diff-5004e2984d28c766f3ec87a77ce07e69797fea8cc36cd753b5ccb182b14e13a2 as that should better cover what a service call usually does since most of them are not going to be callbacks.

I need to think about it a bit more if this behavior change is ok or if its making an existing risk worse.  I agree that your change will make it match the docs, but I'm not sure its actually safe to do given the service call could run forever instead of being cancelled when the connection is closed.  Maybe thats ok though since we already have this problem with automations.

What's I'm having trouble with is that this PR says it restores the behavior of not cancelling the service call when the connection drops, but afaik aiohttp has always cancelled the task when the connection drops (they changed that behavior a few versions ago and we were stuck for a bit before we figured out how to keep the original behavior) so we are talking about a behavior change which is likely to have side effects since service calls didn't need to worry about running forever when called from the api before

This is a significant behavior change which is likely to go unnoticed if we don't highlight it in the release notes.

I think I'm ok with merging this as-is with the test updated and if it's labeled a breaking change.
Also please add a comment about why it's shielded so someone doesn't open a PR in the future to remove it because they were relying on being able to drop the connection to cancel the service call
